body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Stamp file name no longer describes its content**

The file `node_modules/.native-deps-electron-version` now holds `<electron>+patches-<hash>`, not an Electron version. The name appears in rebuild-native.sh, setup-dev.sh, release-desktop.yml and the Windows release spec. Renaming it to something like `.native-deps-stamp` would avoid confusing the next reader. This is optional, since the rename touches several files.

🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Test only checks patched sources, not the compiled binary**

The test reads the C sources in node_modules. Those are patched by `bun install` whether or not `rebuild-native.sh` ran, so it cannot detect the failure that CLAUDE.md calls the trap (patched sources next to an unpatched binary). The stamp checks in setup-dev.sh and the Windows release job cover that case. The macOS release job and `build:mac` have no equivalent stamp check, so the macOS release relies only on the rebuild step not being removed. A stamp check in the macOS job would close that gap.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Out of scope here: the rename touches five files on a high-risk PR for a name that is still accurate as a location (it lives where the old one did and the setup doctor explains its content). Noted as a follow-up: rename to `.native-deps-stamp` together with the next change to these scripts.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of csdev19**

Fixed in d6346e5c: the macOS release job now runs the same stamp check as the Windows job right after `rebuild:native` (Electron version + patch hash), so a dropped or skipped rebuild fails there instead of shipping the unpatched prebuild. On the test: agreed, it pins the patched sources only; the binary is covered by the stamp checks (setup doctor, both release jobs), which is stated in the PR body under "What to review" 5.
